ncertReference.book: CUET General Test / General Science, Breakthroughs & Inventions
ncertReference.chapter: Section 4: Landmark Scientific Discoveries, Nobel Milestones & Indian Scientists

thirtySecondSummary: Science Discoveries evaluates landmark breakthroughs in physics, chemistry, biology, medicine, and astronomy along with legendary inventors and Nobel laureates.
Physical Sciences: Discovery of electron (J.J. Thomson), proton (Ernest Rutherford), neutron (James Chadwick), X-rays (Wilhelm Roentgen), and Radioactivity (Henri Becquerel, Marie Curie).

Biological & Medical Milestones: Discovery of penicillin (Alexander Fleming), DNA double helix (Watson & Crick), vaccination (Edward Jenner - smallpox), circulation of blood (William Harvey), and cell theory (Hooke, Schleiden & Schwann).

Indian Scientific Luminaries: Sir C.V. Raman (Raman Effect - Nobel Prize 1930; National Science Day Feb 28), Jagadish Chandra Bose (crescograph, millimeter radio waves), Homi J. Bhabha (father of Indian nuclear programme), Vikram Sarabhai (father of Indian space programme), and S. Chandrasekhar (Chandrasekhar Limit - 1.4 solar masses).
Modern Frontiers: CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing, mRNA vaccines, James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), and Higgs Boson ('God particle').

coreConcepts.title: Subatomic Particles and Landmark Discoveries in Physics
coreConcepts.explanation:
Fundamental physical discoveries underpinning modern atomic physics:
1. Electron: Discovered by J.J. Thomson in 1897 using cathode ray tube experiments; determined the charge-to-mass ratio (e/m).
2. Proton & Nucleus: Ernest Rutherford discovered the atomic nucleus through the alpha-particle gold foil scattering experiment (1911) and confirmed the proton in 1919.
3. Neutron: Discovered by James Chadwick in 1932 by bombarding beryllium with alpha particles; an uncharged particle with mass slightly greater than a proton.
4. X-Rays & Radioactivity: Wilhelm Conrad Roentgen discovered X-rays in 1895 (first Nobel Prize in Physics, 1901). Henri Becquerel discovered spontaneous radioactivity in uranium salts (1896); Marie and Pierre Curie discovered polonium and radium.
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: NCERT Physics Class XI-XII, Structure of Atom & Nuclei, pp. 1-30.

coreConcepts.title: Medical Breakthroughs, Vaccines, and Biological Milestones
coreConcepts.explanation:
Crucial discoveries that transformed human health and biology:
1. Antibiotics: Alexander Fleming discovered Penicillin in 1928 from the fungus Penicillium notatum, ushering in the antibiotic era (Nobel Prize 1945 with Florey and Chain).
2. Vaccines: Edward Jenner developed the first successful vaccine in 1796 for smallpox using cowpox material, founding the science of immunology.
3. DNA Structure: James Watson and Francis Crick proposed the double-helix model of DNA in 1953 (based on Rosalind Franklin and Maurice Wilkins' X-ray diffraction images).
4. Cell Discovery: Robert Hooke first observed cork cells in 1665 ('Micrographia'); Antonie van Leeuwenhoek observed living microbes ('animalcules').
keyTakeaways: Smallpox Vaccine: Edward Jenner (1796 - father of immunology).
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: NCERT Biology Class XII, Biotechnology & Human Health, pp. 140-180.

coreConcepts.title: Pioneering Indian Scientists and National Institutions
coreConcepts.explanation:
India's rich contribution to world science:
1. Sir C.V. Raman: Discovered the inelastic scattering of light photons by molecules (Raman Effect) on February 28, 1928. Awarded Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930; February 28 is celebrated annually as National Science Day.
2. Dr. Vikram Sarabhai: Established INCOSPAR (1962), which evolved into ISRO (1969); regarded as the 'Father of the Indian Space Programme'.
3. Dr. Homi Jehangir Bhabha: Architect of India's three-stage nuclear power programme; established TIFR and Trombay Atomic Energy Establishment (now BARC).
4. Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar: Formulated the Chandrasekhar Limit (1.44 solar masses), maximum mass for a stable white dwarf star (Nobel Prize in Physics 1983).
keyTakeaways: National Science Day: February 28 (commemorates Raman Effect discovery).
Chandrasekhar Limit: 1.44 times the mass of the Sun.
Father of Indian Space Programme: Vikram Sarabhai.
Father of Indian Nuclear Programme: Homi J. Bhabha.
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: CUET General Knowledge Compendium, Great Indian Scientists, pp. 135-152.

workedExamples.question: Why is February 28 celebrated every year as National Science Day in India?

options.text: It marks the birthday of Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam
It commemorates the discovery of the Raman Effect by Sir C.V. Raman in 1928
It is the founding anniversary of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)
It marks the successful test of Pokhran-I in 1974

solutionStepByStep: Step 1: Recall the historic scientific announcement made on February 28, 1928.
Step 2: Indian physicist Sir Chandrasekhara Venkata Raman discovered the phenomenon of inelastic scattering of light photons, known as the Raman Effect.
Step 3: This discovery won the 1930 Nobel Prize in Physics (first Asian Nobel laureate in science), and in 1986 the Government of India designated February 28 as National Science Day.
workedExamples.cuetInsight: CUET links national days with their exact historical and scientific origins.

workedExamples.question:
Match the subatomic particle with its discoverer:
(P) Electron — 1. J.J. Thomson
(Q) Proton — 2. Ernest Rutherford
(R) Neutron — 3. James Chadwick
solutionStepByStep: Step 1: J.J. Thomson discovered the electron in 1897 via cathode ray tubes -> P-1.
Step 2: Ernest Rutherford discovered the atomic nucleus and proton -> Q-2.
Step 3: James Chadwick proved the existence of uncharged neutrons in 1932 -> R-3.
Step 4: All correspond exactly to option A.

howCuetAsks.typicalStem: Match List-I (Discovery / Invention) with List-II (Scientist): Penicillin, X-Rays, Polio Vaccine, Dynamite.
howCuetAsks.strategy: Penicillin (Fleming), X-Rays (Roentgen), Polio Vaccine (Jonas Salk - injected; Albert Sabin - oral), Dynamite (Alfred Nobel).

howCuetAsks.typicalStem: The crescograph, a device for measuring growth in plants, was invented by which Indian scientist?
howCuetAsks.strategy: Sir Jagadish Chandra Bose invented the crescograph and investigated plant biophysics and microwave radio.

commonTraps.trap: Confusing Jonas Salk and Albert Sabin for Polio vaccine
commonTraps.whyStudentsFail: Both developed polio vaccines; Salk developed the inactivated injectable polio vaccine (IPV, 1955), while Sabin developed the oral polio vaccine (OPV, 1961).
commonTraps.howToAvoid: Remember: Sabin = Sip / Oral drops; Salk = Syringe / Injection.

commonTraps.trap: Thinking C.V. Raman's birthday is Feb 28
commonTraps.whyStudentsFail: Assuming National Science Day is Raman's birthday (his birthday is Nov 7, 1888). Feb 28 is the date the Raman Effect was discovered.
commonTraps.howToAvoid: National Science Day celebrates the DISCOVERY, not the birthday.

practiceQuestions.question: Who among the following discovered Penicillin, the world's first widely effective antibiotic, in 1928?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Sir Alexander Fleming discovered Penicillin in 1928 at St. Mary's Hospital, London, after noticing that the mould Penicillium notatum inhibited bacterial growth.

practiceQuestions.question: The Chandrasekhar Limit, which defines the maximum mass of a stable white dwarf star, is approximately equal to:
practiceQuestions.explanation: Formulated by Indian-American astrophysicist Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar, the limit is approximately 1.44 times the mass of the Sun (M_sun).

practiceQuestions.question: Who discovered the neutron, the neutral subatomic particle present in the atomic nucleus, in 1932?
practiceQuestions.explanation: James Chadwick proved the existence of the neutron by bombarding beryllium atoms with alpha particles, winning the 1935 Nobel Prize in Physics.

practiceQuestions.question: The 'crescograph', a precision sensitive device used to measure growth in plants, was invented by which distinguished Indian polymath?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Sir Jagadish Chandra Bose invented the crescograph in the early 20th century to demonstrate that plants possess cellular responses analogous to animals.

practiceQuestions.question:
Assertion (A): Edward Jenner is revered as the 'Father of Immunology'.
Reason (R): In 1796, Jenner inoculated an eight-year-old boy with cowpox virus to confer immunity against lethal smallpox.

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)

practiceQuestions.explanation: Edward Jenner's pioneering experiment with cowpox created the world's first successful vaccine against smallpox, establishing the foundation of immunology.

practiceQuestions.question:
Match List-I (Invention / Discovery) with List-II (Scientist):
(P) X-Rays — 1. Wilhelm Roentgen
(Q) Polio Vaccine (Injected) — 2. Jonas Salk
(R) Dynamite — 3. Alfred Nobel
(S) Radioactivity — 4. Henri Becquerel
practiceQuestions.explanation: Wilhelm Roentgen discovered X-rays; Jonas Salk developed the first polio vaccine; Alfred Nobel invented dynamite; Henri Becquerel discovered spontaneous radioactivity.

practiceQuestions.question: Who is widely acknowledged as the 'Father of the Indian Space Programme' for spearheading the creation of INCOSPAR and ISRO?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Dr. Vikram Ambalal Sarabhai is celebrated as the Father of the Indian Space Programme, having founded Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station and ISRO.

practiceQuestions.question: In 1953, James Watson and Francis Crick proposed the landmark three-dimensional double-helix structure of which biological macromolecule?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Watson and Crick published their landmark nature paper proposing the antiparallel double-helix model of DNA in April 1953, for which they shared the 1962 Nobel Prize.

practiceQuestions.question: Which particle, predicted by Peter Higgs and François Englert and confirmed at CERN's Large Hadron Collider in 2012, is responsible for imparting mass to elementary particles?
practiceQuestions.explanation: The Higgs boson is the excitation of the Higgs field, which gives mass to fundamental particles such as quarks and charged leptons via the Brout-Englert-Higgs mechanism.

practiceQuestions.question: Who among the following English physicians first correctly described the systemic circulation of blood pumped throughout the body by the heart in 1628?
practiceQuestions.explanation: William Harvey published 'De Motu Cordis' in 1628, providing the first complete and accurate account of the circulatory system and the pumping action of the heart.
